full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J: This appeal is directed against the order dated 6.10.93 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 194 of 1992 rejecting the appellants prayer for temporary injunction and vacating the order of status quo issued earlier. The appellants as plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration of title in the suit land in the 4th Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 194 of 1992, alleging inter alia that the suit land measuring 1.60 acres recorded in the C.S. Plot No. 68 under C.S. Khatian No. 5 corresponding to S.A. Plot No. 68 under S.A. Khatian No. 3 of Mouza 336 Alilbahar P.S. Demra, District Dhaka belonged to their father Nabu Bepari alias Nabu Sheikh. On the death of their father Nabu Bepari they got the suit property by inheritance and since then they have been owning and possessing the same. Further contention of the plaintiffs is that the suit land is low-lying land and mostly it remains under water. The S.A. Khatian was wrongly prepared in the names of Chunnu Miah and Mahbub Elahi and others. The defendants have no title and possession in the suit land. They came to learn recently about the wrong record of right from the local Tahsil Office when they had been there to pay rent. The wrong record of right clouded their title and hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant No. 3 and 6 contested the application for temporary injunction by filing written objection denying all the material allegations of the petition and contended inter alia that Nabu Bepari alias Nabu Sheikh, father of the plaintiffs, lost all his interest in the suit property during his life time by way of sales as well as by acquisition by the Government after which he had no subsisting interest in the suit property. The plaintiffs inherited nothing in the suit property and as such there is no question of recording of their names in the S.A. Khatian. It was further contended that the plaintiffs have had no title and possession in any part of the suit land and they have no prima facie arguable case to get any order of temporary injunction in their favour.
